profile.businessSummary: The Suzlon Group is a leading global renewable energy solutions provider, with approximately 20.8 GW of wind energy capacity installed across 17 countries. It is focused on reducing mankind's carbon footprint by prioritising action today to build climate resilience and undoing the damage of the past and present. As a vertically integrated company, it has in-house R&D centers in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and India, alongside world-class manufacturing facilities spread across India. The company's comprehensive product portfolio is primarily led by its 2 MW and 3 MW series of advanced wind turbines designed for various wind conditions. Suzlon is also India's number one wind energy service company, managing the country's largest service portfolio of over 14.8 GW in wind energy assets. These global wind installations have helped reduce 53.37 million tonnes of CO2 emissions annually, which is equivalent to 4.45 billion trees absorbing CO2.

news.title: Suzlon Energy's 'Suzlon 2.0 Strategy' targets 40% domestic market share by FY31 through expanded product lines. It commissioned 5 MW and 6 MW turbines, pursuing Europe-Australia certification and 50% EPC order mix by FY28.

Suzlon, Trent, and Vedanta Power posted strong quarterly performances, while IndiGo reported its third consecutive quarterly net loss. Blue Star beat profit estimates, Vedanta Oil saw profit dip, and Trent announced Noel Tata's upcoming retirement as chairman.
Suzlon Energy reported a 69.2% YoY drop in Q2 net profit. The company's Q2 revenue increased by 27% YoY.
Suzlon's Q2 EBITDA stood at ₹7.2B, broadly flat compared to ₹7.2B year-on-year. Q2 EBITDA margin contracted to 14.8% from 18.7% year-on-year.

CRISIL upgraded Suzlon Energy's long-term rating to 'CRISIL AA-/Stable' from 'CRISIL A+/Stable'. Short-term rating was upgraded to 'CRISIL A1+' from 'CRISIL A1' for bank facilities totaling Rs 5,685 crore.
Suzlon Energy shares surged over 5% following a report released by Motilal Oswal. The rally positioned the stock among the top gainers in futures trading.
Suzlon share price has dropped 31% over the past three months. Motilal Oswal projects a potential upside of 73% for the stock.

Motilal Oswal maintained a 'buy' on Suzlon Energy with a target of ₹65, implying a 73% upside on attractive valuations. Growth is backed by a 5.9 GW order book, favorable peak power demand, and expanding export and repowering opportunities.
Suzlon Energy plans to set up three new AI-powered factories with an investment of Rs 550 crore.
Suzlon Energy issued a new corporate update via an exchange filing after market hours.
